To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a combination of surprisal and contextual word embeddings is the best model for reconstructing the ERPs, 2) surprisal is more important than contextual embeddings, 3) surprisal models outperform the best contextual embedding models and 4) the best contextual embedding model outperforms the best surprisal model when the surprisal model does not include a language model.
We propose a novel approach to modeling event-related potentials collected during reading that combines pre-trained convolutional neural networks and a language model.
the surprisal model outperforms the word embedding model and that the combination of the two models performs better than either one on its own.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what information is needed to decode ERPs.
the following questions: How well can we reconstruct ERPs from a model of language processing?
the development of a new framework for modeling ERPs and the evaluation of existing sentence processing models using this framework.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best model is a hybrid of the surprisal model with the contextual word embeddings model.
the current best model for ERP decoding is a combination of surprisal and contextual word embedding, but this is not the end of the story.
surprisal and contextual word embedding models are both important for predicting ERPs, and the two together provide a more accurate model of the data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surprisal-based sentence processing models are still the best models for reconstructing event-related potentials.
the best model for decoding ERPs from text is the one that combines surprisal with a language model that is trained on the same data as the model used to compute surprisal.

the neural network models that we tested do not perform well in terms of decoding the ERP signals, but the combination of the neural network and the surprisal model is the best performing model in terms of the correlation between the predicted and actual ERP values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of a language model and a decoder trained on a corpus of sentences is a promising approach for modeling ERPs.

the combination of a pre-trained convolutional decoder and a language model is an effective framework for modeling ERPs, and that this framework can be used to test a variety of sentence processing models.
the best model is not a simple one.
